script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'verif-toolbox-audit',
  description: 'Adversarially audit the Z3 verification toolbox against every requirement clause',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Audit', detail: 'one auditor per requirement dimension' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarially refute each finding' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/workspace'

const FINDINGS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string' },
          file: { type: 'string' },
          line: { type: 'integer' },
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor'] },
          requirement_clause: { type: 'string', description: 'the exact requirement text this violates, or "quality" if none' },
          detail: { type: 'string' },
          repro: { type: 'string', description: 'a concrete python snippet or command that demonstrates the problem' },
        },
        required: ['title', 'file', 'severity', 'requirement_clause', 'detail', 'repro'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['findings'],
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    real: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true only if you actually reproduced or rigorously proved the defect' },
    evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'what you ran and what it printed, or the proof' },
    corrected_severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor', 'not-a-bug'] },
    fix: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete minimal fix if real' },
  },
  required: ['real', 'evidence', 'corrected_severity', 'fix'],
}

const COMMON = [
  'You are auditing a Z3-based verification toolbox at ' + REPO + '. It is a git repo on branch master.',
  '',
  'Ground rules:',
  '- READ-ONLY on tracked source. Do NOT edit any file under ' + REPO + ' except that you MAY create',
  '  scratch scripts under /tmp to reproduce things. Never edit files in ' + REPO + '.',
  '- The requirement contracts are YAML files in ' + REPO + '/requirements/. Read the relevant one(s) IN FULL.',
  '- Run python with: cd ' + REPO + ' && PYTHONPATH=' + REPO + ' python3 -c "..."   (z3 is installed)',
  '- Some CEGAR runs take minutes. Use generous timeouts (e.g. timeout 900).',
  '- Report ONLY defects you can back with a concrete reproduction or a rigorous argument.',
  '  Do NOT report style nits, missing type hints, or "could add more tests".',
  '- A missing API name/signature that the requirement explicitly spells out IS a real finding.',
  '- Prefer few, high-confidence findings over many speculative ones. An empty findings list is a',
  '  perfectly good answer if the code is correct.',
  '',
].join('\n')

const AUDITORS = [
  {
    key: 'traces-validator',
    prompt: COMMON + [
      'Audit dimension: counterexample data structures and the validator.',
      '',
      'Read ' + REPO + '/requirements/cex_minimizer.yaml sections 1 and 2, then',
      REPO + '/verification/cex_minimizer.py.',
      '',
      'Check exhaustively:',
      '- State(values), Transition(src,dst,action), Counterexample(transitions) exist with those',
      '  constructor shapes and the names the requirement uses.',
      '- Counterexample.length property; get_variable_trace(var_name) extracts one variable across',
      '  ALL states (not just transition sources). What happens for an empty trace? For a variable',
      '  absent from some states?',
      '- CEXValidator.validate(cex, init_cond, trans_rel, safety) must: simulate step by step,',
      '  check trans_rel satisfiable with the concrete values per transition, check the initial state',
      '  satisfies init_cond, check the FINAL state violates safety, and return',
      '  ValidationResult(is_real: bool, first_spurious_step: int or None).',
      '- Does first_spurious_step have a sane, documented meaning? Is the ambiguity at index 0',
      '  (init failure vs transition-0 failure) actually handled by consumers correctly?',
      '- Soundness: could validate() return is_real=True for a trace that is NOT a real execution,',
      '  or is_real=False for one that IS? Think about the _bind() helper silently skipping names',
      '  missing from the env or from the state; think about a state that omits a variable the',
      '  relation constrains. Construct concrete adversarial cases and RUN them.',
      '- Note validate() uses satisfiability (not entailment) per step. Since all trace values are',
      '  concrete integers, argue whether sat-vs-entailment matters here. If trans_rel can mention',
      '  a variable NOT pinned by the state (e.g. a nondeterministic input), does using sat make',
      '  validate() too permissive in a way that breaks the CEGAR loop? Test it.',
      '',
      'Return findings.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'refiner',
    prompt: COMMON + [
      'Audit dimension: PredicateRefiner - interpolation and trace minimization.',
      '',
      'Read ' + REPO + '/requirements/cex_minimizer.yaml section 3, then',
      REPO + '/verification/cex_minimizer.py (PredicateRefiner, _image, _interpolate, _walk_path,',
      '_walk_pairs, minimize_cex, _atoms, _plain).',
      '',
      'Check exhaustively:',
      '- extract_interpolants(cex, trans_rel) must be callable with exactly two positional args.',
      '  Does it produce genuinely VALID Craig interpolants? The code claims to verify each candidate',
      '  with "A implies I is valid" and "I and B is unsat". Audit that logic hard: is the local_env',
      '  passed to _interpolate actually the FULL set of A-local variables? If a variable of A is NOT',
      '  in local_env, the "image" is not a projection and I may mention variables absent from B,',
      '  which breaks the interpolant property. Test whether a returned atom can mention a variable',
      '  that does not occur in B.',
      '- The returned predicates are atoms of the interpolant, rewritten over plain names. Is',
      '  splitting an interpolant into atoms sound for predicate abstraction? (It is a standard',
      '  heuristic - only report if you find a concrete way it breaks the CEGAR loop.)',
      '- strengthen_invariant(current_preds, new_interpolants) must merge and remove SUBSUMED',
      '  predicates. Check the direction of subsumption is right and that it never returns a set that',
      '  lost information carried by current_preds. Test with concrete z3 predicates.',
      '- minimize_cex(cex, trans_rel) must never LENGTHEN a trace and must preserve',
      '  "is a real counterexample". Audit each of the five reductions:',
      '  * it MUTATES the list returned by cex.states - verify that does not corrupt the input cex.',
      '  * the safety truncation starts at index 1: can it produce a 0-transition trace, and is that',
      '    still a counterexample? What if the INITIAL state already violates safety?',
      '  * the init-prefix step requires len(states) > 2 - is that off-by-one right?',
      '  * the loop-cut and jump-splice: after splicing, is every remaining step still permitted by',
      '    trans_rel? Write a test that minimizes traces of the 5 experiment systems and then',
      '    RE-VALIDATES the result with CEXValidator, asserting is_real stays True. RUN IT.',
      '  * could stale variable envs leak between the jump-splice SMT queries?',
      '  * confirm empirically that minimize_cex output length is <= input length on many traces.',
      '',
      'Return findings.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'domain',
    prompt: COMMON + [
      'Audit dimension: AbstractDomain predicate abstraction bookkeeping.',
      '',
      'Read ' + REPO + '/requirements/cex_minimizer.yaml section 4, then the AbstractDomain class and',
      'the _rename / _is_trivial / _valid helpers in ' + REPO + '/verification/cex_minimizer.py.',
      '',
      'Check exhaustively:',
      '- The "predicates" attribute, "predicate_count" property, "add_predicate(pred)",',
      '  "is_subsumed(pred_new, pred_existing)" and "abstract_state(concrete_state)" all exist with',
      '  the requirement names and argument order.',
      '- is_subsumed(pred_new, pred_existing): the requirement says "check via SMT if one predicate',
      '  implies another". The code checks Implies(pred_existing, pred_new). Is that the reading that',
      '  makes add_predicate correct? Trace through add_predicate: it rejects pred if',
      '  is_subsumed(pred, known) for some known, and evicts known if is_subsumed(known, pred).',
      '  Verify with concrete predicates (e.g. x>5 vs x>0, x>=0 vs x>=1) that the STRONGER predicate',
      '  is kept and the weaker one dropped, and that the resulting set never loses strength.',
      '  Actually RUN these cases.',
      '- Is add_predicate idempotent? Is the set genuinely irredundant afterwards? Can a sequence of',
      '  adds leave two mutually-subsuming (equivalent but syntactically different) predicates?',
      '- abstract_state(concrete_state) must accept a State AND a plain dict, and evaluate every',
      '  predicate. A predicate that does not reduce to a constant counts False - is that a',
      '  soundness problem for any consumer in this repo? Check who calls abstract_state.',
      '- The "added" and "revision" counters: is "added" a truthful count for the',
      '  CEGAR_PREDICATES_ADDED metric, i.e. does it count admissions and never decrease?',
      '- Predicates are written over plain z3.Int(name) constants and _rename substitutes them.',
      '  What if a predicate mentions a variable NOT in the env passed to _rename? Does the leftover',
      '  plain constant silently alias across steps of an unrolling and thereby make the abstract',
      '  transition relation UNSOUND (too strong, so it could prove an unsafe system safe)? This is',
      '  the most important thing to check in this dimension. Construct a concrete case and run it.',
      '',
      'Return findings.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'loop-soundness',
    prompt: COMMON + [
      'Audit dimension: CEGARLoop / SystemAbstraction soundness and termination.',
      '',
      'Read ' + REPO + '/requirements/cex_minimizer.yaml section 5, then CEGARLoop,',
      'SystemAbstraction, _Conjunct, CEGARResult, build_trace and _unroll in',
      REPO + '/verification/cex_minimizer.py.',
      '',
      'Check exhaustively:',
      '- The __init__ signature must accept (init_cond, trans_rel, safety, max_iterations=20,',
      '  predicate_budget=50) by those names with those defaults.',
      '- CEGARResult must expose safe, iterations, predicates, cex.',
      '- run() must follow the requirement 6 steps and terminate. Both budgets must be enforced:',
      '  is predicate_budget actually checked against something that can exceed it? The check is',
      '  "self.domain.predicate_count > self.predicate_budget" - since subsumption prunes the set,',
      '  can predicate_count ever grow past 50 in practice, i.e. is the budget effectively dead',
      '  code? Would checking domain.added be more faithful to "predicate_budget exceeded"?',
      '  Judge whether this is a real requirement violation and how you would fix it.',
      '- SOUNDNESS (most important): the abstraction must OVER-approximate. If it',
      '  under-approximates, CEGAR could report safe=True for a genuinely unsafe system. Audit:',
      '  * abstract_trans() conjoins kept conjuncts plus preservation constraints. Preservation',
      '    constraints are entailment-checked, so they are implied. Verify that claim empirically.',
      '  * _Conjunct.instantiate substitutes only names present in the passed envs. If a name is',
      '    missing, the ORIGINAL "!c"/"!n" constant survives in the formula. In an unrolling with',
      '    many steps, would that shared leftover constant couple different steps and make the',
      '    relation STRONGER than the concrete one (unsound)? Construct a case (e.g. a system whose',
      '    trans mentions a variable not in the var_names passed to CEGARLoop) and RUN it to see',
      '    whether an unsafe system gets reported safe.',
      '  * collect_var_names(): does it reliably find every variable? Note it swallows exceptions.',
      '    What if init/trans/safety reference a variable only on some code path? If it misses a',
      '    variable, does the pipeline go UNSOUND or merely imprecise? Demonstrate.',
      '- build_trace: it unrolls to EXACTLY horizon steps, then doubles, then tries 1..max_horizon.',
      '  Confirm the fallback loop is reachable and that the function cannot return a trace that is',
      '  not a real path of the ABSTRACT system. Also judge: is the deliberate non-minimality',
      '  honest, or does it inflate CEGAR_CEX_LENGTH_ORIGINAL artificially in a way that',
      '  contradicts the requirement intent ("minimize_cex() produces shorter traces than',
      '  originals")?',
      '- _verify_abstraction: it calls spacer_verifier.verify_transition_system with as_list',
      '  adapters. Verify the adapter maps positional vectors to the right variable names in the',
      '  right ORDER, consistent with how the sorts list is built. An order mismatch would silently',
      '  verify a DIFFERENT system. Test it directly.',
      '- Is there any path where run() loops forever or raises? Check the case where build_trace',
      '  returns None while restore_any() keeps returning an index and spacer keeps saying unsafe.',
      '',
      'Return findings.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'experiment-metrics',
    prompt: COMMON + [
      'Audit dimension: the experiment driver, the 5 systems, the 5 metrics, and run.sh wiring.',
      '',
      'Read ' + REPO + '/requirements/cex_minimizer.yaml sections 6 and Experiments / Instructions /',
      'Files to modify / Acceptance signals, then ' + REPO + '/verification/experiments/cegar_exp.py',
      'and ' + REPO + '/run.sh.',
      '',
      'Check exhaustively:',
      '- The requirement names a CEXMinimizerExperiment. Does it exist? Is it usable?',
      '- The 5 systems must match their descriptions:',
      '  * System 1 counter with off-by-one  -> SAFE AFTER REFINEMENT (iterations must be > 1)',
      '  * System 2 double counter           -> TRULY UNSAFE, real CEX found',
      '  * System 3 array bounds abstraction -> SAFE AFTER 3+ REFINEMENTS',
      '  * System 4 simple loop, invariant x >= 0 -> SAFE IMMEDIATELY (iterations == 1)',
      '  * System 5 producer-consumer buffer overflow -> UNSAFE, NEEDS MINIMIZATION',
      '    (minimized length strictly < original length)',
      '  Run each system and CHECK each claim empirically. Report any mismatch, e.g. if system 3',
      '  needs fewer than 3 refinements, or system 1 is safe on iteration 1.',
      '  Also judge: is System 1 really an "off-by-one counter"? Its safety is x <= 10 with',
      '  limit 10. Is that a faithful reading, and is it safe for the right reason?',
      '  And is System 5 really a "producer-consumer with buffer overflow"?',
      '- Each of the 5 metrics must be emitted exactly once as "KEY: VALUE":',
      '  CEGAR_ITERATIONS, CEGAR_PREDICATES_ADDED, CEGAR_CEX_LENGTH_ORIGINAL,',
      '  CEGAR_CEX_LENGTH_MINIMIZED, CEGAR_VERIFIED_SAFE.',
      '- CEGAR_CEX_LENGTH_MINIMIZED must be strictly less than CEGAR_CEX_LENGTH_ORIGINAL',
      '  ("minimize_cex() produces shorter traces than originals"). Verify.',
      '- CEGAR_VERIFIED_SAFE must be 3 given the system descriptions. Verify.',
      '- run.sh must invoke the CEGAR experiments and must still emit every OTHER layer metric.',
      '  ACTUALLY RUN:  cd ' + REPO + ' && timeout 3000 bash run.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/run_out.txt ; echo "EXIT=$?"',
      '  then confirm all 20 expected keys appear, none is "ERROR: ...", and the exit code is 0.',
      '  The other 15 keys: Z3_NQUEENS_8_SOLUTIONS, Z3_PETERSEN_CHROMATIC, Z3_SCHEDULE_MAKESPAN,',
      '  FP_DAG_REACHABLE_PAIRS, FP_CYCLIC_REACHABLE_PAIRS, FP_HORN_SAFE_COUNT, FP_REACHING_DEFS,',
      '  SPACER_SAFE_SYSTEMS, SPACER_HORN_SAFE, SPACER_BAKERY_SAFE, HORN_CLAUSES_GENERATED,',
      '  HORN_PROGRAMS_VERIFIED, HORN_PROGRAMS_UNSAFE, HORN_LOOP_INVARIANTS,',
      '  HORN_TRANSLATION_TIME.',
      '- Report the total wall-clock time run.sh takes. If it exceeds ~25 minutes, flag it as a',
      '  MAJOR finding (harness timeout risk) and say which system dominates.',
      '- Determinism: run the cegar experiment TWICE and report whether the 5 metric values are',
      '  identical. Non-determinism in reported metrics is a major finding.',
      '',
      'Return findings.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'regression-other-layers',
    prompt: COMMON + [
      'Audit dimension: regression check on the four ALREADY-COMPLETED requirements.',
      '',
      'The repo has committed implementations for requirements z3, uz_fixedpoint, spacer and',
      'horn_translator. There is ALSO an uncommitted modification to',
      REPO + '/verification/horn_translator.py (see: cd ' + REPO + ' && git diff).',
      '',
      'Your job:',
      '1. Read requirements/z3.yaml, requirements/uz_fixedpoint.yaml, requirements/spacer.yaml and',
      '   requirements/horn_translator.yaml IN FULL.',
      '2. For each, confirm every named function/class/signature in the requirement actually exists',
      '   with that name. Specifically confirm these exist and are callable:',
      '   - smt_solver: count_nqueens_solutions, chromatic_number, schedule_jobs,',
      '     run_z3_experiments',
      '   - fixedpoint: count_reachable_pairs, check_horn_safety, analyze_reaching_definitions,',
      '     run_fixedpoint_experiments',
      '   - spacer_verifier: verify_transition_system(name, state_sorts, init_cond, trans_rel,',
      '     safety_prop), verify_horn_file, build_counter_system, build_bakery_system,',
      '     build_double_inc_system, run_spacer_experiments',
      '   - verification.horn_translator: Variable, Const, BinOp, Assign, If, While, Assert,',
      '     Sequence, parse_program, HornEncoder (encode_program, encode_assignment, encode_loop,',
      '     encode_branch, encode_assertion, to_z3), HornVerifier and/or verify_program,',
      '     HornTranslatorExperiment',
      '   Report any that are MISSING or whose signature contradicts the requirement.',
      '3. Review the uncommitted git diff to horn_translator.py adversarially. It adds an',
      '   _ensure_state() helper so encode_* methods work standalone, an arity check in _apply,',
      '   and changes to_z3 so discovered program_vars are ALWAYS declared. Does that diff BREAK',
      '   anything? In particular:',
      '   - does to_z3(program_vars=[...]) still behave sanely for existing callers?',
      '   - could always-declaring self.program_vars turn a previously-ground rule into a',
      '     quantified one and change a verification verdict?',
      '   - is the arity check reachable in normal operation, i.e. does it now raise where it',
      '     used to work?',
      '   You must not edit files, but you CAN run the current state and reason about the diff.',
      '4. Run these and report exact output:',
      '   cd ' + REPO + ' && PYTHONPATH=' + REPO + ' timeout 900 python3 -m agent_tests.test_units',
      '   cd ' + REPO + ' && PYTHONPATH=' + REPO + ' timeout 900 python3 -m agent_tests.test_horn',
      '   Report every FAIL line verbatim. A failing check here is a BLOCKER finding.',
      '',
      'Return findings.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
]

phase('Audit')
log('auditing ' + AUDITORS.length + ' dimensions of the verification toolbox')

const perDimension = await pipeline(
  AUDITORS,
  a => agent(a.prompt, { label: 'audit:' + a.key, phase: 'Audit', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA }),
  (res, a) => {
    const findings = (res && res.findings) || []
    if (!findings.length) return []
    return parallel(findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(COMMON + [
        'You are an adversarial VERIFIER. Another agent claims the following defect in the',
        'verification toolbox at ' + REPO + '. Your default assumption is that it is WRONG.',
        '',
        'CLAIM: ' + f.title,
        'FILE: ' + f.file + (f.line ? ':' + f.line : ''),
        'SEVERITY CLAIMED: ' + f.severity,
        'REQUIREMENT CLAUSE CLAIMED VIOLATED: ' + f.requirement_clause,
        'DETAIL: ' + f.detail,
        'CLAIMED REPRO: ' + f.repro,
        '',
        'Do this:',
        '1. Read the cited code yourself.',
        '2. Read the cited requirement clause in ' + REPO + '/requirements/ and quote it. If the',
        '   claim misreads the requirement, that alone makes it not-a-bug.',
        '3. ACTUALLY RUN the repro (adapt it if it is sloppy, but do not weaken it). Paste what it',
        '   printed.',
        '4. Decide: real=true ONLY if you reproduced the defect or can prove it rigorously.',
        '   If the claimed repro does not reproduce, real=false.',
        '5. If real, give the minimal concrete fix.',
        '',
        'Be skeptical. "The code could be clearer" is not-a-bug. "A named API the requirement',
        'spells out is genuinely absent" IS a bug. Set real=false if uncertain.',
      ].join('\n'),
        { label: 'verify:' + a.key + ':' + f.title.slice(0, 40), phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA })
        .then(v => ({ dimension: a.key, finding: f, verdict: v }))
    ))
  }
)

const all = perDimension.flat().filter(Boolean)
const confirmed = all.filter(x => x.verdict && x.verdict.real && x.verdict.corrected_severity !== 'not-a-bug')

log(all.length + ' candidate findings, ' + confirmed.length + ' survived adversarial verification')

return {
  totalCandidates: all.length,
  confirmed: confirmed.map(x => ({
    dimension: x.dimension,
    title: x.finding.title,
    file: x.finding.file,
    line: x.finding.line,
    severity: x.verdict.corrected_severity,
    requirement_clause: x.finding.requirement_clause,
    detail: x.finding.detail,
    evidence: x.verdict.evidence,
    fix: x.verdict.fix,
  })),
  refuted: all.filter(x => confirmed.indexOf(x) === -1).map(x => ({
    dimension: x.dimension,
    title: x.finding.title,
    why: x.verdict ? x.verdict.evidence : 'verifier failed',
  })),
}
